extracted.intended_audience: authors, peer reviewers, and editors of Springer Nature journals
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher-level editorial and ethical policies for submitting, reviewing, and publishing manuscripts in Springer Nature journals, covering authorship, disclosures, peer review, corrections, data and reporting standards, AI use, and related practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate with respect
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff, authors, reviewers and the public must behave professionally and respectfully; aggressive behaviour, harassment, bullying or discrimination is not tolerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature reserves the right to bring serious cases to employers or authorities, refuse interaction or business with repeat/serious violators, and expects mutual respect to build trust and quality publishing products and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship definition (authorship principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors whose names appear must have made substantial contributions to conception/design, data acquisition/analysis/interpretation, or creation of new software; drafted or critically revised the work; approved the version to be published; and agree to be accountable for all aspects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher does not prescribe contribution types; authors should follow field-specific guidelines (e.g., ICMJE). Contributors not meeting all criteria should be listed in Acknowledgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship clarified — consent and institutional approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature assumes all authors agreed with the content, gave explicit consent to submit, and obtained consent from responsible authorities at the institute/organisation where the work was carried out before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are strongly advised to ensure correct author group, corresponding author and author order at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures and declarations required
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must include information on sources of funding, financial or non-financial interests, ethics committee approval (human/animal), informed consent for human participants, and animal welfare statements as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether such info should be included depends on journal scope and article type; when in doubt include appropriate disclosures. See also 'Summary of requirements' for placement in a Declarations section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are requested to ensure all data, materials, and software/code supporting published claims comply with field standards and support the published claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may have individual (sharing) policies; check Instructions for Authors. Authors should make data and code available according to disciplinary norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the Corresponding Author
rubrics_metrics.description: One author is assigned as Corresponding Author who acts on behalf of all co-authors and ensures questions related to accuracy or integrity are appropriately addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include ensuring all authors approved the manuscript and names/order, managing communications between journal and co-authors, providing transparency on reuse/unpublished material, and ensuring disclosures are included. Managing communication may be delegated to a Contact or Submitting Author if Corresponding Author is clearly indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author contribution statements encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals encourage transparency by publishing author contribution statements specifying the contribution of every author; some journals allow statements of equal contribution or joint supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Level of detail varies by discipline; contributors who contributed equally or jointly supervised can be labelled; check journal Instructions for Authors for format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary affiliation should be the institution where the majority of the work was done; current address may also be stated if the author has moved; affiliations are not updated after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure names are correctly spelled and addresses/affiliations are current at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should ensure correct author group and order at submission. Changes to the author list after submission must be approved by every author; adding/deleting authors at revision is generally not permitted and changes cannot be made after acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If changes are warranted during revision, reasons must be explained and approval is at Editor-in-Chief discretion; journals may have individual policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author name change (inclusive name change policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who changed their name (e.g., gender transition or religious conversion) may request corrections to published papers and can choose a silent correction (no public note) or a formal public Author Correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer provides a contact form for inclusive name change requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author identification (ORCID recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly recommended to use or acquire an ORCID ID when submitting an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORCID helps identify authors and is recommended during submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deceased or incapacitated authors
rubrics_metrics.description: If a co-author dies or is incapacitated during writing, submission, or peer-review, co-authors may include them with approval from a (legal) representative such as a direct relative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain appropriate approval from a legal representative where inclusion is deemed appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should treat all communication with the Journal — including correspondence with Editors and reviewers' reports — as confidential unless explicit consent to share is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality applies before and after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship disputes policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal is not in a position to adjudicate authorship disputes during peer review or after acceptance; authors are asked to resolve disputes themselves. If unable, the Journal may withdraw a manuscript or raise the issue with authors' institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may act (withdraw manuscript) if dispute unresolved; follow institutional guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests disclosure scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must disclose interests directly or indirectly related to the submitted work, including funding, employment, financial interests (stocks, patents, consultancy), and non-financial interests (editorial board positions, consulting, expert witness, mentoring relations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report interests within the last 3 years of beginning the work; disclose older interests if they could reasonably be perceived as influencing the work. Disclosure helps readers judge potential bias and is not necessarily disqualifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of requirements — Declarations section
rubrics_metrics.description: The above disclosures should be summarized in a 'Declarations' section before the reference list, including headings such as Funding, Conflicts of interest/Competing interests, Ethics approval, Consent, Data and/or Code availability and Authors’ contribution statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the information already appears elsewhere (e.g., Methods), repeat it here. Templates and example wording are provided; a blanket statement suffices when all authors have same (or no) conflicts/funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibilities — originality and simultaneous submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript should not be submitted to more than one publication simultaneously and should be original and not previously published in any form (unless expansion or translation with transparency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid text-recycling/self-plagiarism and salami-slicing; provide transparency on reuse of material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibilities — data integrity and image manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Results must be presented clearly and honestly without fabrication, falsification or inappropriate data manipulation, including image-based manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should adhere to discipline-specific rules for acquiring/selecting/processing data; journals may use software to screen for plagiarism and may request original data or images to verify validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibilities — plagiarism and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: No data, text, or theories by others should be presented as the author's own; proper acknowledgements, quotation marks for verbatim copying, and permissions for copyrighted material are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism screening software may be used; ensure permissions for software, questionnaires, surveys and scales where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibilities — literature citation practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and non-research articles must cite appropriate and relevant literature to support claims; excessive or inappropriate self-citation or coordinated self-citation is strongly discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid untrue statements about entities or personal attacks. For review articles (authoritative), disclosure statements are required. Use discipline norms for citation coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical responsibilities — dual-use and biosecurity
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that may be misapplied to pose a threat to public health or national security should be clearly identified (dual use), e.g., biological agents, vaccine disruption, chemical hazards, weaponization of research/technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should identify such risks in the manuscript; editors may handle these cases specially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation outcomes for suspected misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: If misconduct is suspected and an investigation finds valid concerns, possible actions include rejection if under consideration, correction, editorial expression of concern, or retraction if published. The author’s institution may be informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retractions are neutral tools to correct the literature; retraction notices are indexed and linked to the original article which is watermarked 'retracted'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors must correct fundamental errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are obligated to correct significant errors or inaccuracies once discovered and contact the journal to explain how the error impacts the article; corrections or retractions will be decided accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction notes should provide transparency about impacted parts of the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting and excluding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may suggest suitable reviewers and/or request exclusion of certain individuals (usually a maximum of two); suggested reviewers must be independent and not connected to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide institutional email addresses or other identity-verifying information (homepage, publication record, researcher ID). Editors are not obliged to use suggestions; each manuscript should be reviewed by at least one reviewer not suggested by the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation integrity — unacceptable practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Unethical citation practices (citation manipulation, excessive self-citation, irrelevant or non-existent/hallucinated references) breach integrity policies and may lead to rejection or retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use citations to support statements, have read cited sources, cite original work where possible, aim for diverse sources, avoid excessive citations for one point, prefer peer-reviewed sources, avoid adverts/advertorials, and include DOIs where possible. Carefully review citations after AI use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint sharing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting preprints of primary research on preprint servers, authors' or institutional websites is encouraged and is not considered prior publication; preprints may be posted at any time during peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose preprint DOI and licensing upon submission; update preprint records with publication references after journal publication. Authors may choose any license for preprints; follow guidance on communications with media and avoid implying peer review status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections, retractions and matters arising — corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors that affect accuracy but do not substantially invalidate conclusions may be corrected via a published Correction linked to the original article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections are indexed and bidirectionally linked; name-change corrections have a separate policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections, retractions and matters arising — retractions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the interpretation or conclusion of an article is substantially undermined, retraction may be necessary; editorial decisions to retract are based on reliability and confidence in interpretation/conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer follows COPE guidelines; retraction notices are neutral, indexed, linked, and the article is watermarked as retracted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial notes and expressions of concern
rubrics_metrics.description: An Editor’s Note alerts readers that an inquiry has been initiated (online-only, not indexed). An Editorial Expression of Concern (EEoC) alerts readers to serious concerns affecting integrity; EEoCs are indexed, receive a DOI and may be interim or final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EEoCs keep readers updated during investigations and may be superseded by corrections or retractions once investigations conclude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of published content
rubrics_metrics.description: In exceptional circumstances Springer Nature may remove content when it is defamatory, infringes legal rights, unlawful, subject to court/government order, or poses immediate serious health risk; bibliographic metadata will be retained with an explanatory statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal may be temporary or permanent and is used only in exceptional conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and complaints process
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals against editorial decisions, complaints about process failures (e.g., delays), and complaints about publication ethics should be raised first with the Editor-in-Chief/Handling Editor or in-house publishing contact; unresolved matters may be escalated to ethics.reporting@springernature.com or COPE for ethics complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For appeals about rejection, the Editor will consider the authors’ argument, reviewer reports, and may (a) uphold rejection, (b) seek another independent opinion, or (c) consider the appeal; decisions are final and new submissions take priority over appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predatory journals caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should assess carefully whether material from questionable/'predatory' journals should be referenced; predatory journals often solicit authors with flattering spam and may mimic names of reputable journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer points to OASPA, DOAJ and COPE resources and notes indexing services are scrutinising predatory practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI authorship and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) do not satisfy authorship criteria and cannot be listed as authors; use of LLMs must be properly documented in Methods or an appropriate section. AI-assisted copy-editing (grammar/style/readability) need not be declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There must be human accountability for the final version and agreement from authors that edits reflect their original work. Generative AI images are generally not permitted except in limited exceptions and must be labelled as AI-generated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI by peer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers should not upload manuscripts into generative AI tools due to limitations and potential confidentiality breaches; if AI tools support any part of evaluation, reviewers should declare such use in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are exploring safe AI tools for reviewers, but peer reviewers remain accountable for reports and should avoid sharing manuscript content with external generative AI services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital image integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Images must not be inappropriately manipulated; journals may request original image files and use screening tools to detect manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must follow ethical and legal standards for images; examples of covered image types include video, photography, scientific diagrams, photo-illustrations and collages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of reporting and mandatory checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature advocates complete and transparent reporting; for biomedical and biological research, certain checklists must be completed before peer review and made available to editors and reviewers (e.g., CONSORT, SPIRIT, PRISMA, CARE, ARRIVE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional encouraged guidelines include STROBE, PRISMA-P, STARD, TRIPOD, AGREE, RIGHT, SRQR, COREQ, SQUIRE, CHEERS depending on study type; check journal requirements for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review — general policy
rubrics_metrics.description: All research articles and most other article types undergo peer review, usually by at least two independent expert reviewers; submissions are first checked for completeness then assessed by an Editor for suitability for peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual journals may differ in process (open/double-anonymized). Editors consider peer review reports but are not bound by them; a single reviewer concern may lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer selection is based on expertise, reputation, recommendations, conflicts of interest and previous performance; institutional email addresses should be used where possible and reviewer identity verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each manuscript should be reviewed by at least one reviewer not suggested by the author; editors should independently verify suggested reviewers' contact details and request disclosure of possible conflicts before accepting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum reviewer requirements and exceptional cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors are expected to obtain a minimum of two peer reviewers for primary research; in exceptional circumstances (niche/emerging fields) one reviewer may suffice if the report meets standards. If two independent reviewers cannot be secured, the Editor may act as a second reviewer or make a decision using one report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Editor acts as second reviewer they must have sufficient knowledge, sign the review for transparency, and any single reports should be detailed and thorough. The first reviewer should be senior, on-topic and have recent publications on the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer guidance — principles of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should adhere to COPE ethical guidelines: be objective, avoid personal criticism, express views clearly with supporting arguments/references, declare competing interests, and respect confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential comments to the Editor are welcome but must not contradict the report to authors. Reviewers should decline if they have competing interests and should not pass invitations to colleagues without contacting the journal first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer guidance — assessment components
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to comment on key results, validity (flaws that should prohibit publication), originality/significance, data & methodology (including supplementary info), appropriate use of statistics, conclusions robustness, inflammatory/libelous material, suggested improvements, references, clarity and context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should specify parts outside their expertise, address editor's specific questions, ensure error bars and statistical tests are described properly, and check adherence to Sex and Gender in Research (SAGER) guidelines where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer tone, professionalism and report quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting, reviewers should ensure the report tone is courteous and professional, avoid unnecessary personal remarks, and remove inappropriate language; reports should document thought process and provide justification for statements with facts and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may remove inappropriate language from reports. Reports need not follow a strict order but should help editors reach fair, evidence-based decisions and help authors improve manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer timeliness and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should respond promptly within the number of days agreed and notify the journal if delays are anticipated so alternatives can be found and authors kept informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely reviews support rapid editorial decisions and publication; reviewers are encouraged to balance speed with thoroughness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer diversity and inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should consider diversity, equity and inclusion when inviting reviewers, including geographical region, gender identities, and racial/ethnic groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature is committed to diverse demographic representation among reviewers and asks reviewers to flag concerns affecting this commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer misconduct and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Fraudulent behaviour such as identity theft or suggesting fake reviewers will result in manuscript rejection, investigation per misconduct policy, and notification to authors’ institutions/employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer journals are COPE members; reviewer fraud/falsification resources are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review models defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review models include Open peer review (names published with reports), Transparent peer review (reports published without reviewer names), Single-anonymized (reviewers anonymous to authors) and Double-anonymized (neither party knows the other's identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications are mediated by the Editor; pre-publication histories may not always be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer Nature offers reviewers the opportunity to credit their ORCID profile with verified peer review data transmitted directly from the submission system at the time of report submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This forms part of reviewer appreciation and recognition programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collections and special issues — standard editorial criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to collections or special issues are assessed according to the journal’s standard editorial criteria and subject to standard editorial policies including competing interests and scope of the collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review for special issues follows the journal's standard process; submissions for which editors have competing interests are handled by another editor with no competing interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act with integrity (general conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: All staff and researchers engaging with Springer Nature must uphold honesty, accountability, fairness and legal/ethical compliance; breaches may lead to withdrawal of manuscripts or post-publication actions and reporting to authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer may refuse to interact or do business with individuals who repeatedly or seriously violate these principles and will investigate suspected breaches.
